\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{غسل} \ur{خانہ} (ghusl khānā)}{غسل خانہ (ghusl khānā)}]{\ur{غسل} \ur{خانہ} (ghusl khānā) — a washroom; a bathroom}

\label{lesson:UR-C404-ghusl-khana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to spread out (a sheet), then the Urdu for a lift.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{غسل} \ur{خانہ}}
\textbf{\ur{غسل} \ur{خانہ}} — \emph{ghusl khānā} — \textquotedblleft{}a washroom; a bathroom\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کمرے} \ur{کے} \ur{ساتھ} \ur{ایک} \ur{غسل} \ur{خانہ} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kamre ke sāth ek ghusl khānā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is a washroom next to the room.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{غسل} \ur{خانہ}} (\emph{ghusl khānā}) is built from \emph{ghusl}, \textquotedblleft{}washing\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{ghusl}, and Persian \emph{khāna}, \textquotedblleft{}a house, a room\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghusl khānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kamre ke sāth ek ghusl khānā hai.} — There is a washroom next to the room.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to spread out (a sheet), then the Urdu for a lift, then say \emph{ghusl khānā} again
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گیزر}}
